endorsements.quote: Ensure commercial interests do not override patient and public safety.
Fund and conduct prospective clinical trials and RCTs d .
Establish continuous monitoring pipelines for model drift.
Use RAG e and grounding in trusted medical databases.
Develop interpretable models or integrate XAI b methods.
Operationalize AI literacy programs for clinicians.
Use only diverse, inclusive, and representative datasets.
Ensure routine equity audits during deployment.
Understand the limitations of AI in the patient care spectrum.

unlisted_practices: Establish formal GenAI leadership roles to ensure ethical and equitable use.
Operationalize clear sunset policies for unsafe models.
Require human-in-the-loop verification of AI outputs.
Ensure physicians and nurses take full responsibility for patient safety regardless of AI tool use.
Require developers to sign a conflict of interest declaration form.
Co-design model explanations with clinicians and patients.
Apply fairness-aware machine learning techniques such as reweighting and adversarial debiasing.
Implement common data standards and interoperability across health data systems.
Implement stress testing for dataset shift.
Implement active learning and regular retraining of deployed models.
Conduct pilot testing of AI tools in real-world clinical workflows.
Adopt human-centered design for AI tools and integrate them with EHR workflows.
Reduce the environmental impact of AI through energy-efficient architectures and carbon accounting.
Establish independent ethics boards for objective oversight of AI.
Governments and foundations should financially support GenAI adoption by community clinics and resource-limited settings.
Incorporate hands-on AI training into health professional curricula.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/perspective discussing ethical challenges, governance, and next steps for generative AI adoption and deployment in health care.
